3dbd38c43bbc6600.prompt:
You choose the one UI component that best fits a need on a phone app screen.
Components:
- Actions: Two to four shortcuts to different things the person can do next. Pick: Two to four separate navigation shortcuts together, such as logging, adding and viewing a schedule. Not independent jobs to tick off (Checklist), one main action (Button), or records to browse (List).
- Amount: One sum of money written properly, with its period, old price or change. Pick: One sum of money is the point: a balance, a price, a total or what is owed. Not several figures side by side (Stats), the screen's headline in words (Hero), or the price on each row of a list (List).
- Banner: Something important to notice now, with an optional link to act. Pick: An immediate warning or status update that stands out at the top. Not a supporting sentence (Note), the screen's main statement (Hero) or a panel with more detail (Sheet).
- Bars: Compare counts or amounts across days or categories, using the actual counted or measured unit. Pick: Compare one amount across days or categories. Not a few separate summary numbers (Stats), a trend with its latest value (Sparkline) or progress toward targets (Progress).
- Bubbles: A conversation between you and someone else, with each person's messages kept distinct. Pick: Show an exchange between you and another person, keeping who said each message clear. Not things to browse and tap (List) or one supporting sentence without a reply (Note).
- Button: One main thing the person does next. Pick: One labelled action to press. Not two to four shortcuts (Actions) or a tappable summary of one thing (Card).
- Calendar: See which dates have something planned and open a day. Pick: Days of a week or month, with dates marked for planned activity. Not events with times in order (Timeline) or separate things to browse (List).
- Camera: Aim at something and take a new picture or scan its code. Pick: Take a new picture or scan a code while aiming at the subject. Not showing an existing picture (Photo), or adding a picture to a labelled form value (Field).
- Canvas: An idea no existing component can express, such as a game or a drawing tool. Pick: Only choose Canvas for an idea no other component can express, such as an interactive game or a drawing tool. Not a message about missing content (Empty), or an existing image to display (Photo).
- Card: One thing with a little detail, optionally tappable to open it. Pick: A compact preview of one thing, with a title and short detail, optionally opening it. Not several separate things to scan (List) or the screen's main headline (Hero).
- Checklist: Things to do, with each job ticked off when done. Pick: Tick off independent jobs. Not browsing and opening things (List) or following an ordered sequence (Steps).
- Chips: Filter things or pick one value from a few short options. Pick: Filter a collection or choose a value. Not switching between views (Segmented), ticking off jobs (Checklist) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- Choice: Choose among two to five options that each need a sentence to explain. Pick: Choosing among a few options that each carry a short explanation, such as a plan, an answer to a question or a way of doing something. Not one-word filters (Chips), a short value inside a form (Field), switching views of one screen (Segmented), or keep-or-skip one at a time (SwipeStack).
- Composer: Write several lines of text: an entry, a note, a review or a reply. Pick: Writing more than one line, such as a journal entry, a note, a review or a reply under a conversation. Not one short value on a form (Field), or finding something by name (Search).
- Counter: Increase or decrease one running count by a fixed step with each tap. Pick: One count whose plus button increments and minus button decrements the number by a fixed step. Not several read-only summary numbers (Stats) or a number entered in a form (Field).
- Empty: A calm message on a screen that has no content yet. Pick: Only when there is no content or no results yet, explaining their absence. Not the screen's main statement about what exists or needs attention (Hero), a separate warning or status notice (Banner), or a supporting sentence (Note).
- Field: Enter or change one labelled piece of information on a form. Pick: Enter one named value, such as a name, date, amount or form choice. Not finding things by typing a query (Search), standalone collection filters and quick choices (Chips), several lines of writing (Composer) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- Gallery: Browse several pictures together, optionally opening one. Pick: Several pictures to browse together, in a grid or sideways strip. Not one picture on its own (Photo) or text-led rows of separate things (List).
- Header: Name the screen and offer one optional shortcut. Pick: The title at the top of a screen. Not a label above a group (SectionTitle) or the screen's main message (Hero).
- Hero: The screen's main statement or headline number, including what needs attention today. Pick: The screen's main message, photo-led introduction or headline number, even when it says something needs attention. Not a separate urgent alert or status update (Banner), a supporting sentence (Note), several numbers (Stats) or one sum of money as the point (Amount).
- KeyValue: Label and value details of one single thing, like its room or schedule. Pick: Any need about one thing's details or settings. Not several separate things (List) or summary numbers (Stats).
- List: Several things of the same kind, each one tappable. Pick: Several things of one kind to scan and tap individually, even when asked to tap just one of them. Not one featured thing (Card), details of one thing (KeyValue), or jobs to tick off (Checklist).

- Camera: Aim at something to take a photo, record video, or scan it. Pick: Aim at a subject to take a new picture, record video, scan a code or capture both sides of a document. Not showing an existing picture (Photo), or adding a picture to a labelled form value (Field).
- Canvas: An idea no existing component can express, such as a game or a drawing tool. Pick: Only choose Canvas for an idea no other component can express, such as an interactive game or a drawing tool. Not a message about missing content (Empty), or an existing image to display (Photo).
- Card: One thing with a little detail, optionally tappable to open it. Pick: A compact preview of one thing, with a title and short detail, optionally opening it. Not several separate things to scan (List) or the screen's main headline (Hero).
- Checklist: Things to do, with each job ticked off when done. Pick: Tick off independent jobs. Not browsing and opening things (List) or following an ordered sequence (Steps).
- Chips: Filter things or pick one value from a few short options. Pick: Filter a collection or choose a value. Not switching between views (Segmented), ticking off jobs (Checklist) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- Choice: Choose among two to five options that each need a sentence to explain. Pick: Choosing among a few options that each carry a short explanation, such as a plan, an answer to a question or a way of doing something. Not one-word filters (Chips), a short value inside a form (Field), switching views of one screen (Segmented), or keep-or-skip one at a time (SwipeStack).
- Composer: Write several lines of text: an entry, a note, a review or a reply. Pick: Writing more than one line, such as a journal entry, a note, a review or a reply under a conversation. Not one short value on a form (Field), or finding something by name (Search).
- Counter: Increase or decrease one running count by a fixed step with each tap. Pick: One count whose plus button increments and minus button decrements the number by a fixed step. Not several read-only summary numbers (Stats) or a number entered in a form (Field).
- Empty: A calm message on a screen that has no content yet. Pick: Only when there is no content or no results yet, explaining their absence. Not the screen's main statement about what exists or needs attention (Hero), a separate warning or status notice (Banner), or a supporting sentence (Note).
- Field: Enter or change one labelled piece of information on a form. Pick: Enter one named value, such as a name, date, amount or form choice. Not finding things by typing a query (Search), standalone collection filters and quick choices (Chips), several lines of writing (Composer) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- Gallery: Browse several pictures together, optionally opening one. Pick: Several pictures to browse together, in a grid or sideways strip. Not one picture on its own (Photo) or text-led rows of separate things (List).
- Header: Name the screen and offer one optional shortcut. Pick: The title at the top of a screen. Not a label above a group (SectionTitle) or the screen's main message (Hero).
- Hero: The screen's main statement or headline number, including what needs attention today. Pick: The screen's main message, photo-led introduction or headline number, even when it says something needs attention. Not a separate urgent alert or status update (Banner), a supporting sentence (Note), several numbers (Stats) or one sum of money as the point (Amount).
- KeyValue: Label and value details of one single thing, like its room or schedule. Pick: Any need about one thing's details or settings. Not several separate things (List) or summary numbers (Stats).
- List: Several things of the same kind, each one tappable. Pick: Show all the person's entries of one kind so they can scan and tap them, even if they will open only one. Not one featured thing (Card), pictures to browse (Gallery), details of one record (KeyValue), or jobs to tick off (Checklist).
- MapPins: See where nearby places are and open a place. Pick: Places positioned on a map, with matching numbered labels and optional links. Not places visited in travel order (Route) or things to browse without their locations on a map (List).
- Note: One short sentence of supporting information. Pick: Add a short supporting sentence. Not something to notice now (Banner), the screen's main statement (Hero) or text the person writes (Composer).
- People: Who else is involved, with their names and roles. Pick: A plain roster of people: several participants, teammates, clients or family members, with names and optional photos or roles. Choose this even for just names and photos, without roles, links or turn controls. Not general non-person records (List) or one person's identity block (Profile).
- Photo: Show one picture, with an optional caption. Pick: One picture on its own, optionally captioned. Not several pictures (Gallery) or a photo-led main message with a headline (Hero).
- Player: Listen to or watch one recording, with play, skip and a scrubber. Pick: One recording to listen to or watch now, such as a meditation, a lesson, an episode, an exercise video or a voice memo. Not a list of recordings to choose from (List), one picture (Photo), or timing an activity with no recording (Timer).
- Profile: Identify the person, pet or plant whose screen this is. Pick: An identity block with a name, short detail and optional portrait. Not a screen title or navigation (Header), or a summary to open another thing (Card).
- Progress: Progress toward several targets at once, each bar with its amount and target. Pick: Several measured amounts, each against its own target, such as macros, a budget per category or lessons per course. Not one main goal (Ring), amounts compared with each other (Bars), or place in a short sequence (Steps).
- Ring: How far you are toward one goal. Pick: One amount completed toward a target. Not several targets at once (Progress), several summary numbers (Stats) or ordered stages of a process (Steps).
- Route: Follow a path between places, from the first stop to the last. Pick: Show places visited in travel order, with an optional total distance. Not events ordered by time (Timeline) or locations positioned on a map without a visiting order (MapPins).
- Scale: Log a rating or feeling from one to five. Pick: Rate how something went, feels or looks on five ordered levels. Not switching views (Segmented) or entering information in a general input (Field).
- Search: Find one thing among many by typing words from its name. Pick: Type a query above a list to find matching things. Not a few fixed filters (Chips), entering one piece of information (Field) or writing several lines (Composer).
- SectionTitle: Label a group of content and offer one optional link to more. Pick: A short label just above a group within a screen. Not the screen's title at the top (Header) or its main message (Hero).
- Segmented: Switch between two to four views of the same screen. Pick: One active view of the same screen, such as today or week. Not filters or choices among values (Chips), or navigation between screens (TabBar).
- Sheet: A panel over the screen for more detail, a longer pick or a few extra actions. Pick: More about one thing without leaving the screen, picking from six or more options, or a few extra actions behind the header. Not a message that stays on the screen (Banner), two to five options shown inline (Choice, Chips), or a whole new task (a new screen).
- Sparkline: See how one measurement is changing, alongside its latest value. Pick: One latest value with its recent rise or fall. Not separate amounts per day or category to compare (Bars), or several summary numbers (Stats).
- Stats: Two to four independent summary numbers, with labels, units and optional change arrows. Pick: Several independent summary measurements shown together, with an optional change arrow on each. Not amounts compared across days or categories (Bars), one latest measurement with its recent line (Sparkline), one record's details (KeyValue), one headline number (Hero), or one sum of money (Amount).
- Steps: Know your current place in a short ordered flow. Pick: Show the current position in a short setup or booking flow. Not independent jobs to tick off (Checklist) or progress toward a numeric goal (Ring).
- Streak: How many days in a row you kept a habit, with this week's completed days. Pick: Consecutive days of a habit with daily completion this week. Not several independent totals (Stats) or your position in an ordered flow (Steps).
- Success: Know an action worked, with its result and the saved item's details. Pick: A standalone moment after an action worked, with a result title and optional detail. Not an ongoing status or urgent warning at the top (Banner), or a screen with no content yet (Empty).
- SwipeStack: Choose between things one at a time, swiping the current one to keep or skip. Pick: Decide which of several things to keep or skip, one at a time. Swipe only the top choice. Not browsing several captioned pictures together (Gallery) or opening a single featured preview (Card).
- Timeline: Events in time order, or activities sized by duration on an hour rail. Pick: Dated or timed events in order. Use hours when start/end times, duration and free gaps matter. Not choosing dates (Calendar), things without times to browse (List), or independent jobs (Checklist).
- Timer: Measure time remaining or elapsed, with controls to start and stop. Pick: Time remaining until an activity ends or elapsed since it began. Not a number manually nudged up or down (Counter) or an amount completed toward a goal (Ring).
- Cart: Review and edit what you are about to buy. Pick: One shopping basket before ordering, with editable quantities, removal, a promo code and computed totals. Not browsing several past orders (List), a receipt for one placed order (OrderSummary), or a grocery checklist (GroceryList).
- CartBar: Return to a nonempty basket from a shopping screen. Pick: A persistent bottom shortcut to the basket with its live count and total, hidden when empty. Not a lone action without live basket data (Button) or the editable basket itself (Cart).
- Checkout: Choose fulfillment and payment, then place an order. Pick: Finish a goods order by choosing pickup or delivery and a payment method, then place it. Not editing one field (Field), reviewing an appointment (Appointment), or editing basket items (Cart).
- OrderStatus: Follow an order through fulfillment or move it along as the seller. Pick: Track fulfillment milestones on one goods order, with timestamps and a seller's next-stage action. Not a multi-step form (Steps), a map (DeliveryTracker), or an order receipt (OrderSummary).
- OrderSummary: See what was ordered, what it cost and how it will arrive. Pick: A receipt for one placed goods order with quantities and fulfillment details. Not simple facts (KeyValue), the editable basket (Cart), fulfillment progress (OrderStatus), or a client bill (Invoice).
- Product: Decide whether to buy one product and add the desired quantity. Pick: One product for sale with a description, stock, saving or quantity and add controls. Not a price alone (Amount), several products (ProductGrid), or a timed service (ServiceMenu).
- ProductGrid: Browse products with prices and quickly add the ones you want. Pick: Browse several priced goods with a quick add per product, as photo cards or food menu rows. Not photos without prices (Gallery), timed services (ServiceMenu), or owned things (Things).
- Promo: Notice an offer, copy its discount code or open the offer. Pick: A shop discount or offer with optional copyable code, expiry and product photo. Not an urgent warning or service notice (Banner) or a headline fact (Hero).
- SavedList: Track saved shop products, compare prices, and move items to the basket. Pick: A shop wishlist for saved buy-later products with saved versus current prices, drop alerts, a move-to-cart action, or shared gift claims. Not already in the basket (Cart), ordinary saved links (List), owned stock (Things), or an event registry (Registry).
- SizeGuide: Compare product measurements and fit across sizes before choosing one. Pick: Compare garment or footwear measurements across sizes, switch centimetres and inches, and check how the product fits. Not facts about a single item (KeyValue), a generic data grid (Table), or choosing a purchasable option (VariantPicker).
- VariantPicker: Choose an available size, colour or other option for one product. Pick: Select the variant of one product, with optional price differences and disabled unavailable options. Not choosing a plan (Choice) or filtering a product list (Chips).

Write one complete phone screen as JSON: {id,title?,components:[{id,c,...props}]}. Use unique snake_case ids for components; never put ids on array items. Use only listed props. Use null for absent optional fields, never write empty strings.

Layout: shop/saved. Job: Browse goods for sale.

Brief: Review products I saved for later, see any price changes, and move products into my basket.
Return compact JSON. When a layout says to omit a field the schema requires, write null for it instead.

Recipe slots: [{"id":"slot_0","allow":["Header"],"min":1,"max":1},{"id":"slot_1","allow":["SavedList"],"min":1,"max":1},{"id":"slot_2","allow":["CartBar"],"min":1,"max":1}]. Match every required slot in order. Variants such as shelf, reply, month or mood are the component's style; Field/Camera variants are kind. prices means every Choice option has a price value; toggle means every List row has trail: toggle.

Screen rules: three to nine components outside overlays, total weight at most twelve, at most two weight-three components. One primary Button at most. Hero first in the body; a SectionTitle needs following content. Repeated types cannot be adjacent except Card and Field. Reply Composer is last after Bubbles. Do not invent color, size or layout props.

Set shared axes, including item axes, only when explicitly requested; otherwise use null. At most one third of items per component get mark "highlight" (round down).
density: comfortable|compact
emphasis: quiet|normal|hero
surface: plain|card|tinted|outlined
align: start|center
bleed: inset|edge
aspect: auto|square|wide|tall
detail: full|brief
media: none|icon|thumb|cover
figures: exact|short
labels: key|none|all
arrange: rows|grid|strip
group: none|sections|dates
overflow: all|peek|page
lead: none|icon|avatar|thumb|number|check
trail: none|chevron|value|badge|toggle|check
tone: neutral|good|warn|bad
mark: none|highlight|muted|new

An explicit layout rule can request an axis. Catalog examples show JSON shape, not requested styling. Never infer an axis from the data alone. Variant limits: one hero emphasis and one cover collection per screen.

Real app content: {"things":[],"items":[]}

Header: Name the screen and offer one optional shortcut.
props: { density?: comfortable|compact, emphasis?: normal|quiet="normal", detail?: full|brief="full", style?: back, title: text≤28, sub?: text≤40, action?: { icon: dot|leaf|drop|dog|cat|calendar|calendar_days|clock|check|chevron_right|plus|minus|close|search|settings|bell|bell_off|heart|star|bookmark|share|send|message|mail|phone|camera|image|video|mic|music|play|pause|square|undo|timer|alarm_clock|sun|moon|cloud|cloud_rain|thermometer|wind|flame|zap|battery|wifi|pin|map|navigation|compass|home|building|store|shopping_cart|shopping_bag|tag|gift|credit_card|wallet|banknote|piggy_bank|receipt|trending_up|trending_down|bar_chart|pie_chart|activity|target|trophy|medal|award|flag|user|users|user_plus|baby|smile|dumbbell|bike|footprints|heart_pulse|pill|stethoscope|apple|coffee|utensils|wine|pizza|carrot|sprout|flower|tree|mountain|waves|car|bus|plane|train|briefcase|graduation_cap|book_open|book|pencil|file_text|clipboard|clipboard_list|checklist|lock|unlock|key|shield|eye|link|paperclip|download|upload|trash|edit|filter|sliders|info|alert|help|sparkles|lightbulb|palette|scissors|wrench|hammer|package|truck|recycle|globe|languages|gamepad|ticket|paw|shirt|bed|bath|sofa|lamp|chevron_left|arrow_left|more|external_link|quote|circle_check, label: text≤16, goto?: id snake_case } }
Rule: Use style "back" only when a back button is needed. To hide a subtitle, use detail "brief" and keep the supplied subtitle in sub. Hiding it does not request a smaller title or a denser header: set emphasis and density to null unless the brief explicitly asks for those changes.
example: {"c":"Header","title":"My plants","sub":"Three need water today","action":{"icon":"plus","label":"Add a plant","goto":"new_plant"}}
weight: 1

SavedList: Track saved shop products, compare prices, and move items to the basket.
props: { items: [1..12 { id: text≤24, name: text≤28, photo?: photo lib:<tag>|local:<n>, price: num 0..99999.99, savedPrice?: num 0..99999.99, targetPrice?: num 0..99999.99, stock?: int 0..9007199254740991, claimed?: boolean=false, goto?: id snake_case }], shared?: boolean=false, arrange?: rows|grid="rows", density?: comfortable|compact, surface?: card|plain="card" }
Rule: Use a distinct short product id per item, including items without a link. Use numeric prices without a currency sign. Only write stock when known and never write computed badges.
Rule: Set shared true only for a shared gift list. For two columns set arrange "grid"; use null for unrequested density and surface, never explicit defaults.
example: {"c":"SavedList","items":[{"id":"fern_pot","name":"Glazed fern pot","photo":"lib:fern","price":12,"savedPrice":16,"targetPrice":11,"stock":8,"goto":"fern"},{"id":"basil_planter","name":"Basil planter","photo":"lib:basil","price":10,"savedPrice":10,"stock":2}]}
weight: 3

CartBar: Return to a nonempty basket from a shopping screen.
props: { goto: id snake_case, density?: comfortable|compact, emphasis?: normal|quiet="normal" }
Rule: Supply the basket screen id in goto. The host supplies the basket count and total.
example: {"c":"CartBar","goto":"plant_supplies"}
weight: 2

An "=value" in the props list is a render default, not a value to output. Never copy a variant from an example. Leave emphasis null unless the request asks to change prominence, even if "normal" is listed.

Density changes spacing only. Use null to inherit app spacing unless the request asks for tighter or roomier spacing. Showing fewer rows, hiding details, and shortening text do not change spacing.

Keep requested content visible. Leave detail null when the default already shows the requested content, or when there is no extra content to hide. Set detail only if the request asks to hide or reveal existing content and the default does not do that. Read-only changes actions, not visibility.

Use the supplied facts, not content from examples. Do not invent dates, status, measurements, or zero values for missing data. Keep all components focused on the screen's job; give the main action a clear label and avoid duplicate or unrelated actions. If a list explains a chart, show the corresponding details in chart order. For a grouped or filtered list, make instructions and action destinations clear enough to follow without guessing. Reply with JSON only.

bleed: inset|edge

figures: exact|short
labels: key|none|all
arrange: rows|grid|strip

overflow: all|peek|page

- Banner: Something important to notice now, with an optional link to act. Pick: An immediate warning or status update that stands out at the top. Not a supporting sentence (Note), the screen's main statement (Hero) or a panel with more detail (Sheet).
- Bars: Compare counts or amounts across days or categories, using the actual counted or measured unit. Pick: Compare one amount across days or categories. Not a few separate summary numbers (Stats), a trend with its latest value (Sparkline) or progress toward targets (Progress).
- Bubbles: A conversation between you and someone else, with each person's messages kept distinct. Pick: Show an exchange between you and another person, keeping who said each message clear. Not things to browse and tap (List) or one supporting sentence without a reply (Note).
- Button: One main thing the person does next. Pick: One labelled action to press. Not two to four shortcuts (Actions) or a tappable summary of one thing (Card).
- Calendar: See which dates have something planned and open a day. Pick: Days of a week or month, with dates marked for planned activity. Not events with times in order (Timeline) or separate things to browse (List).
- Camera: Aim at something to take a photo, record video, or scan it. Pick: Aim at a subject to take a new picture, record video, scan a code or capture both sides of a document. Not showing an existing picture (Photo), or adding a picture to a labelled form value (Field).
- Canvas: An idea no existing component can express, such as a game or a drawing tool. Pick: Only choose Canvas for an idea no other component can express, such as an interactive game or a drawing tool. Not a message about missing content (Empty), or an existing image to display (Photo).
- Card: One thing with a little detail, optionally tappable to open it. Pick: A compact preview of one thing, with a title and short detail, optionally opening it. Not several separate things to scan (List) or the screen's main headline (Hero).
- Checklist: Things to do, with each job ticked off when done. Pick: Tick off independent jobs. Not browsing and opening things (List) or following an ordered sequence (Steps).
- Chips: Filter things or pick one value from a few short options. Pick: Filter a collection or choose a value. Not switching between views (Segmented), ticking off jobs (Checklist) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- Choice: Choose among two to five options that each need a sentence to explain. Pick: Choosing among a few options that each carry a short explanation, such as a plan, an answer to a question or a way of doing something. Not one-word filters (Chips), a short value inside a form (Field), switching views of one screen (Segmented), or keep-or-skip one at a time (SwipeStack).
- Composer: Write several lines of text: an entry, a note, a review or a reply. Pick: Writing more than one line, such as a journal entry, a note, a review or a reply under a conversation. Not one short value on a form (Field), or finding something by name (Search).
- Counter: Increase or decrease one running count by a fixed step with each tap. Pick: One count whose plus button increments and minus button decrements the number by a fixed step. Not several read-only summary numbers (Stats) or a number entered in a form (Field).
- Empty: A calm message on a screen that has no content yet. Pick: Only when there is no content or no results yet, explaining their absence. Not the screen's main statement about what exists or needs attention (Hero), a separate warning or status notice (Banner), or a supporting sentence (Note).
- Field: Enter or change one labelled piece of information on a form. Pick: Enter one named value, such as a name, date, amount or form choice. Not finding things by typing a query (Search), standalone collection filters and quick choices (Chips), several lines of writing (Composer) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- FileList: Show attached files and let people preview, download, or remove them. Pick: One to six non-image file attachments with names, formats and sizes, for example PDFs, contracts, spreadsheets, ZIPs or audio files. Not photos (Gallery or Photo), general list records (List), a file explorer (DriveTree or FileBrowser), or an ID vault (Documents).
- Gallery: Browse several pictures together, optionally opening one. Pick: Several pictures to browse together, in a grid or sideways strip. Not one picture on its own (Photo) or text-led rows of separate things (List).
- Header: Name the screen and offer one optional shortcut. Pick: The title at the top of a screen. Not a label above a group (SectionTitle) or the screen's main message (Hero).
- Hero: The screen's main statement or headline number, including what needs attention today. Pick: The screen's main message, photo-led introduction or headline number, even when it says something needs attention. Not a separate urgent alert or status update (Banner), a supporting sentence (Note), several numbers (Stats) or one sum of money as the point (Amount).
- KeyValue: Label and value details of one single thing, like its room or schedule. Pick: Any need about one thing's details or settings. Not several separate things (List) or summary numbers (Stats).
- List: Several things of the same kind, each one tappable. Pick: Show all the person's entries of one kind so they can scan and tap them, even if they will open only one. Not one featured thing (Card), pictures to browse (Gallery), details of one record (KeyValue), or jobs to tick off (Checklist).
- MapPins: See where nearby places are and open a place. Pick: Places positioned on a map, with matching numbered labels and optional links. Not places visited in travel order (Route) or things to browse without their locations on a map (List).
- Note: One short sentence of supporting information. Pick: Add a short supporting sentence. Not something to notice now (Banner), the screen's main statement (Hero) or text the person writes (Composer).
- PassCard: Keep a membership, coupon, or transit pass ready to show and scan. Pick: A digital membership card, coupon, insurance ID or transit fare pass with a code to show or scan. Not ordinary details of one record without a pass (KeyValue), an event admission ticket (Ticket or EventPass), a travel itinerary (Reservation), or a full tier and reward wallet (RewardsWallet).

- Photo: Show one picture, with an optional caption. Pick: One picture on its own, optionally captioned. Not several pictures (Gallery) or a photo-led main message with a headline (Hero).
- Player: Listen to or watch one recording, with play, skip and a scrubber. Pick: One recording to listen to or watch now, such as a meditation, a lesson, an episode, an exercise video or a voice memo. Not a list of recordings to choose from (List), one picture (Photo), or timing an activity with no recording (Timer).
- Profile: Identify the person, pet or plant whose screen this is. Pick: An identity block with a name, short detail and optional portrait. Not a screen title or navigation (Header), or a summary to open another thing (Card).
- Progress: Progress toward several targets at once, each bar with its amount and target. - SectionTitle: Label a group of content and offer one optional link to more. Pick: A short label just above a group within a screen. Not the screen's title at the top (Header) or its main message (Hero).
- Segmented: Switch between two to four views of the same screen. Pick: One active view of the same screen, such as today or week. Not filters or choices among values (Chips), or navigation between screens (TabBar).
- Sheet: A panel over the screen for more detail, a longer pick or a few extra actions. Pick: More about one thing without leaving the screen, picking from six or more options, or a few extra actions behind the header. Not a message that stays on the screen (Banner), two to five options shown inline (Choice, Chips), or a whole new task (a new screen).
- Sparkline: See how one measurement is changing, alongside its latest value. Pick: One latest value with its recent rise or fall. Not separate amounts per day or category to compare (Bars), or several summary numbers (Stats).

- Banner: Something important to notice now, with an optional link to act. Pick: An immediate warning or status update that stands out at the top. Not a supporting sentence (Note), the screen's main statement (Hero) or a panel with more detail (Sheet).
- Bars: Compare counts or amounts across days or categories, using the actual counted or measured unit. Pick: Compare one amount across days or categories. Not a few separate summary numbers (Stats), a trend with its latest value (Sparkline) or progress toward targets (Progress).
- Bubbles: A conversation between you and someone else, with each person's messages kept distinct. Pick: Show an exchange between you and another person, keeping who said each message clear. Not things to browse and tap (List) or one supporting sentence without a reply (Note).
- Button: One main thing the person does next. Pick: One labelled action to press. Not two to four shortcuts (Actions) or a tappable summary of one thing (Card).
- Calendar: See which dates have something planned and open a day. Pick: Days of a week or month, with dates marked for planned activity. Not events with times in order (Timeline) or separate things to browse (List).
- Camera: Aim at something to take a photo, record video, or scan it. Pick: Aim at a subject to take a new picture, record video, scan a code or capture both sides of a document. Not showing an existing picture (Photo), or adding a picture to a labelled form value (Field).
- Canvas: An idea no existing component can express, such as a game or a drawing tool. Pick: Only choose Canvas for an idea no other component can express, such as an interactive game or a drawing tool. Not a message about missing content (Empty), or an existing image to display (Photo).
- Card: One thing with a little detail, optionally tappable to open it. Pick: A compact preview of one thing, with a title and short detail, optionally opening it. Not several separate things to scan (List) or the screen's main headline (Hero).
- Checklist: Things to do, with each job ticked off when done. Pick: Tick off independent jobs. Not browsing and opening things (List) or following an ordered sequence (Steps).
- Chips: Filter things or pick one value from a few short options. Pick: Filter a collection or choose a value. Not switching between views (Segmented), ticking off jobs (Checklist) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- Choice: Choose among two to five options that each need a sentence to explain. Pick: Choosing among a few options that each carry a short explanation, such as a plan, an answer to a question or a way of doing something. Not one-word filters (Chips), a short value inside a form (Field), switching views of one screen (Segmented), or keep-or-skip one at a time (SwipeStack).
- Composer: Write several lines of text: an entry, a note, a review or a reply. Pick: Writing more than one line, such as a journal entry, a note, a review or a reply under a conversation. Not one short value on a form (Field), or finding something by name (Search).
- Counter: Increase or decrease one running count by a fixed step with each tap. Pick: One count whose plus button increments and minus button decrements the number by a fixed step. Not several read-only summary numbers (Stats) or a number entered in a form (Field).
- Empty: A calm message on a screen that has no content yet. Pick: Only when there is no content or no results yet, explaining their absence. Not the screen's main statement about what exists or needs attention (Hero), a separate warning or status notice (Banner), or a supporting sentence (Note).
- Field: Enter or change one labelled piece of information on a form. Pick: Enter one named value, such as a name, date, amount or form choice. Not finding things by typing a query (Search), standalone collection filters and quick choices (Chips), several lines of writing (Composer) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- Gallery: Browse several pictures together, optionally opening one. Pick: Several pictures to browse together, in a grid or sideways strip. Not one picture on its own (Photo) or text-led rows of separate things (List).
- Header: Name the screen and offer one optional shortcut. Pick: The title at the top of a screen. Not a label above a group (SectionTitle) or the screen's main message (Hero).
- Hero: The screen's main statement or headline number, including what needs attention today. Pick: The screen's main message, photo-led introduction or headline number, even when it says something needs attention. Not a separate urgent alert or status update (Banner), a supporting sentence (Note), several numbers (Stats) or one sum of money as the point (Amount).
- KeyValue: Label and value details of one single thing, like its room or schedule. Pick: Any need about one thing's details or settings. Not several separate things (List) or summary numbers (Stats).
- List: Several things of the same kind, each one tappable. Pick: Show all the person's entries of one kind so they can scan and tap them, even if they will open only one. Not one featured thing (Card), pictures to browse (Gallery), details of one record (KeyValue), or jobs to tick off (Checklist).
- MapPins: See where nearby places are and open a place. Pick: Places positioned on a map, with matching numbered labels and optional links. Not places visited in travel order (Route) or things to browse without their locations on a map (List).
- Note: One short sentence of supporting information. Pick: Add a short supporting sentence. Not something to notice now (Banner), the screen's main statement (Hero) or text the person writes (Composer).
- People: Who else is involved, with their names and roles. Pick: A plain roster of people: several participants, teammates, clients or family members, with names and optional photos or roles. Choose this even for just names and photos, without roles, links or turn controls. Not general non-person records (List) or one person's identity block (Profile).
- Photo: Show one picture, with an optional caption. Pick: One picture on its own, optionally captioned. Not several pictures (Gallery) or a photo-led main message with a headline (Hero).
- Player: Listen to or watch one recording, with play, skip and a scrubber. Pick: One recording to listen to or watch now, such as a meditation, a lesson, an episode, an exercise video or a voice memo. Not a list of recordings to choose from (List), one picture (Photo), or timing an activity with no recording (Timer).
- Profile: Identify the person, pet or plant whose screen this is. Pick: An identity block with a name, short detail and optional portrait. Not a screen title or navigation (Header), or a summary to open another thing (Card).
- Progress: Progress toward several targets at once, each bar with its amount and target. Pick: Several measured amounts, each against its own target, such as macros, a budget per category or lessons per course. Not one main goal (Ring), amounts compared with each other (Bars), or place in a short sequence (Steps).
- Ring: How far you are toward one goal. Pick: One amount completed toward a target. Not several targets at once (Progress), several summary numbers (Stats) or ordered stages of a process (Steps).
- Route: Follow a path between places, from the first stop to the last. Pick: Show places visited in travel order, with an optional total distance. Not events ordered by time (Timeline) or locations positioned on a map without a visiting order (MapPins).
- Scale: Log a rating or feeling from one to five. Pick: Rate how something went, feels or looks on five ordered levels. Not switching views (Segmented) or entering information in a general input (Field).
- Search: Find one thing among many by typing words from its name. Pick: Type a query above a list to find matching things. Not a few fixed filters (Chips), entering one piece of information (Field) or writing several lines (Composer).
- SectionTitle: Label a group of content and offer one optional link to more. Pick: A short label just above a group within a screen. Not the screen's title at the top (Header) or its main message (Hero).
- Segmented: Switch between two to four views of the same screen. Pick: One active view of the same screen, such as today or week. Not filters or choices among values (Chips), or navigation between screens (TabBar).
- Sheet: A panel over the screen for more detail, a longer pick or a few extra actions. Pick: More about one thing without leaving the screen, picking from six or more options, or a few extra actions behind the header. Not a message that stays on the screen (Banner), two to five options shown inline (Choice, Chips), or a whole new task (a new screen).
- Sparkline: See how one measurement is changing, alongside its latest value. Pick: One latest value with its recent rise or fall. Not separate amounts per day or category to compare (Bars), or several summary numbers (Stats).
- Stats: Two to four independent summary numbers, with labels, units and optional change arrows. Pick: Several independent summary measurements shown together, with an optional change arrow on each. Not amounts compared across days or categories (Bars), one latest measurement with its recent line (Sparkline), one record's details (KeyValue), one headline number (Hero), or one sum of money (Amount).
- Steps: Know your current place in a short ordered flow. Pick: Show the current position in a short setup or booking flow. Not independent jobs to tick off (Checklist) or progress toward a numeric goal (Ring).
- Streak: How many days in a row you kept a habit, with this week's completed days. Pick: Consecutive days of a habit with daily completion this week. Not several independent totals (Stats) or your position in an ordered flow (Steps).
- Success: Know an action worked, with its result and the saved item's details. Pick: A standalone moment after an action worked, with a result title and optional detail. Not an ongoing status or urgent warning at the top (Banner), or a screen with no content yet (Empty).
- SwipeStack: Choose between things one at a time, swiping the current one to keep or skip. Pick: Decide which of several things to keep or skip, one at a time. Swipe only the top choice. Not browsing several captioned pictures together (Gallery) or opening a single featured preview (Card).
- Timeline: Events in time order, or activities sized by duration on an hour rail. Pick: Dated or timed events in order. Use hours when start/end times, duration and free gaps matter. Not choosing dates (Calendar), things without times to browse (List), or independent jobs (Checklist).
- Timer: Measure time remaining or elapsed, with controls to start and stop. Pick: Time remaining until an activity ends or elapsed since it began. Not a number manually nudged up or down (Counter) or an amount completed toward a goal (Ring).
- Cart: Review and edit what you are about to buy. Pick: One shopping basket before ordering, with editable quantities, removal, a promo code and computed totals. Not browsing several past orders (List), a receipt for one placed order (OrderSummary), or a grocery checklist (GroceryList).
- CartBar: Return to a nonempty basket from a shopping screen. Pick: A persistent bottom shortcut to the basket with its live count and total, hidden when empty. Not a lone action without live basket data (Button) or the editable basket itself (Cart).
- Checkout: Choose fulfillment and payment, then place an order. Pick: Finish a goods order by choosing pickup or delivery and a payment method, then place it. Not editing one field (Field), reviewing an appointment (Appointment), or editing basket items (Cart).
- OrderStatus: Follow an order through fulfillment or move it along as the seller. Pick: Track fulfillment milestones on one goods order, with timestamps and a seller's next-stage action. Not a multi-step form (Steps), a map (DeliveryTracker), or an order receipt (OrderSummary).
- OrderSummary: See what was ordered, what it cost and how it will arrive. Pick: A receipt for one placed goods order with quantities and fulfillment details. Not simple facts (KeyValue), the editable basket (Cart), fulfillment progress (OrderStatus), or a client bill (Invoice).
- Product: Decide whether to buy one product and add the desired quantity. Pick: One product for sale with a description, stock, saving or quantity and add controls. Not a price alone (Amount), several products (ProductGrid), or a timed service (ServiceMenu).
- ProductGrid: Browse products with prices and quickly add the ones you want. Pick: Browse several priced goods with a quick add per product, as photo cards or food menu rows. Not photos without prices (Gallery), timed services (ServiceMenu), or owned things (Things).

53716c5e923f0ab1.prompt:
You choose the one UI component that best fits a need on a phone app screen.
Components:
- Actions: Two to four shortcuts to different things the person can do next. Pick: Two to four separate navigation shortcuts together, such as logging, adding and viewing a schedule. Not independent jobs to tick off (Checklist), one main action (Button), or records to browse (List).
- Amount: One sum of money written properly, with its period, old price or change. Pick: One sum of money is the point: a balance, a price, a total or what is owed. Not several figures side by side (Stats), the screen's headline in words (Hero), or the price on each row of a list (List).
- Banner: Something important to notice now, with an optional link to act. Pick: An immediate warning or status update that stands out at the top. Not a supporting sentence (Note), the screen's main statement (Hero) or a panel with more detail (Sheet).
- Bars: Compare counts or amounts across days or categories, using the actual counted or measured unit. Pick: Compare one amount across days or categories. Not a few separate summary numbers (Stats), a trend with its latest value (Sparkline) or progress toward targets (Progress).
- Bubbles: A conversation between you and someone else, with each person's messages kept distinct. Pick: Show an exchange between you and another person, keeping who said each message clear. Not things to browse and tap (List) or one supporting sentence without a reply (Note).
- Button: One main thing the person does next. Pick: One labelled action to press. Not two to four shortcuts (Actions) or a tappable summary of one thing (Card).
- Calendar: See which dates have something planned and open a day. Pick: Days of a week or month, with dates marked for planned activity. Not events with times in order (Timeline) or separate things to browse (List).
- Camera: Aim at something and take a new picture or scan its code. Pick: Take a new picture or scan a code while aiming at the subject. Not showing an existing picture (Photo), or adding a picture to a labelled form value (Field).
- Canvas: An idea no existing component can express, such as a game or a drawing tool. Pick: Only choose Canvas for an idea no other component can express, such as an interactive game or a drawing tool. Not a message about missing content (Empty), or an existing image to display (Photo).
- Card: One thing with a little detail, optionally tappable to open it. Pick: A compact preview of one thing, with a title and short detail, optionally opening it. Not several separate things to scan (List) or the screen's main headline (Hero).
- Checklist: Things to do, with each job ticked off when done. Pick: Tick off independent jobs. Not browsing and opening things (List) or following an ordered sequence (Steps).
- Chips: Filter things or pick one value from a few short options. Pick: Filter a collection or choose a value. Not switching between views (Segmented), ticking off jobs (Checklist) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- Choice: Choose among two to five options that each need a sentence to explain. Pick: Choosing among a few options that each carry a short explanation, such as a plan, an answer to a question or a way of doing something. Not one-word filters (Chips), a short value inside a form (Field), switching views of one screen (Segmented), or keep-or-skip one at a time (SwipeStack).
- Composer: Write several lines of text: an entry, a note, a review or a reply. Pick: Writing more than one line, such as a journal entry, a note, a review or a reply under a conversation. Not one short value on a form (Field), or finding something by name (Search).
- Counter: Increase or decrease one running count by a fixed step with each tap. Pick: One count whose plus button increments and minus button decrements the number by a fixed step. Not several read-only summary numbers (Stats) or a number entered in a form (Field).
- Empty: A calm message on a screen that has no content yet. Pick: Only when there is no content or no results yet, explaining their absence. Not the screen's main statement about what exists or needs attention (Hero), a separate warning or status notice (Banner), or a supporting sentence (Note).
- Field: Enter or change one labelled piece of information on a form. Pick: Enter one named value, such as a name, date, amount or form choice. Not finding things by typing a query (Search), standalone collection filters and quick choices (Chips), several lines of writing (Composer) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- Gallery: Browse several pictures together, optionally opening one. Pick: Several pictures to browse together, in a grid or sideways strip. Not one picture on its own (Photo) or text-led rows of separate things (List).
- Header: Name the screen and offer one optional shortcut. Pick: The title at the top of a screen. Not a label above a group (SectionTitle) or the screen's main message (Hero).
- Hero: The screen's main statement or headline number, including what needs attention today. Pick: The screen's main message, photo-led introduction or headline number, even when it says something needs attention. Not a separate urgent alert or status update (Banner), a supporting sentence (Note), several numbers (Stats) or one sum of money as the point (Amount).
- KeyValue: Label and value details of one single thing, like its room or schedule. Pick: Any need about one thing's details or settings. Not several separate things (List) or summary numbers (Stats).
- List: Several things of the same kind, each one tappable. Pick: Several things of one kind to scan and tap individually, even when asked to tap just one of them. Not one featured thing (Card), details of one thing (KeyValue), or jobs to tick off (Checklist).
- MapPins: See where nearby places are and open a place. Pick: Places positioned on a map, with matching numbered labels and optional links. Not places visited in travel order (Route) or things to browse without their locations on a map (List).
- Note: One short sentence of supporting information. Pick: Add a short supporting sentence. Not something to notice now (Banner), the screen's main statement (Hero) or text the person writes (Composer).
- People: Who else is involved, with their names and roles. Pick: The clients, family or team involved, with a name and optional role for each person. Not general things to scan and tap (List), or the identity of one screen's subject (Profile).
- Photo: Show one picture, with an optional caption. Pick: One picture on its own, optionally captioned. Not several pictures (Gallery) or a photo-led main message with a headline (Hero).
- Player: Listen to or watch one recording, with play, skip and a scrubber. Pick: One recording to listen to or watch now, such as a meditation, a lesson, an episode, an exercise video or a voice memo. Not a list of recordings to choose from (List), one picture (Photo), or timing an activity with no recording (Timer).
- Profile: Identify the person, pet or plant whose screen this is. Pick: An identity block with a name, short detail and optional portrait. Not a screen title or navigation (Header), or a summary to open another thing (Card).
- Progress: Progress toward several targets at once, each bar with its amount and target. Pick: Several measured amounts, each against its own target, such as macros, a budget per category or lessons per course. Not one main goal (Ring), amounts compared with each other (Bars), or place in a short sequence (Steps).
- Ring: How far you are toward one goal. Pick: One amount completed toward a target. Not several targets at once (Progress), several summary numbers (Stats) or ordered stages of a process (Steps).
- Route: Follow a path between places, from the first stop to the last. Pick: Show places visited in travel order, with an optional total distance. Not events ordered by time (Timeline) or locations positioned on a map without a visiting order (MapPins).
- Scale: Log a rating or feeling from one to five. Pick: Rate how something went, feels or looks on five ordered levels. Not switching views (Segmented) or entering information in a general input (Field).
- Search: Find one thing among many by typing words from its name. Pick: Type a query above a list to find matching things. Not a few fixed filters (Chips), entering one piece of information (Field) or writing several lines (Composer).
- SectionTitle: Label a group of content and offer one optional link to more. Pick: A short label just above a group within a screen. Not the screen's title at the top (Header) or its main message (Hero).
- Segmented: Switch between two to four views of the same screen. Pick: One active view of the same screen, such as today or week. Not filters or choices among values (Chips), or navigation between screens (TabBar).
- Sheet: A panel over the screen for more detail, a longer pick or a few extra actions. Pick: More about one thing without leaving the screen, picking from six or more options, or a few extra actions behind the header. Not a message that stays on the screen (Banner), two to five options shown inline (Choice, Chips), or a whole new task (a new screen).
- Sparkline: See how one measurement is changing, alongside its latest value. Pick: One latest value with its recent rise or fall. Not separate amounts per day or category to compare (Bars), or several summary numbers (Stats).
- Stats: Two to four independent summary numbers, with labels, units and optional change arrows. Pick: Several independent summary measurements shown together, with an optional change arrow on each. Not amounts compared across days or categories (Bars), one latest measurement with its recent line (Sparkline), one record's details (KeyValue), one headline number (Hero), or one sum of money (Amount).
- Steps: Know your current place in a short ordered flow. Pick: Show the current position in a short setup or booking flow. Not independent jobs to tick off (Checklist) or progress toward a numeric goal (Ring).
- Streak: How many days in a row you kept a habit, with this week's completed days. Pick: Consecutive days of a habit with daily completion this week. Not several independent totals (Stats) or your position in an ordered flow (Steps).
- Success: Know an action worked, with its result and the saved item's details. Pick: A standalone moment after an action worked, with a result title and optional detail. Not an ongoing status or urgent warning at the top (Banner), or a screen with no content yet (Empty).
- SwipeStack: Choose between things one at a time, swiping the current one to keep or skip. Pick: Decide which of several things to keep or skip, one at a time. Swipe only the top choice. Not browsing several captioned pictures together (Gallery) or opening a single featured preview (Card).
- Timeline: Events in time order, or activities sized by duration on an hour rail. Pick: Dated or timed events in order. Use hours when start/end times, duration and free gaps matter. Not choosing dates (Calendar), things without times to browse (List), or independent jobs (Checklist).
- Timer: Measure time remaining or elapsed, with controls to start and stop. Pick: Time remaining until an activity ends or elapsed since it began. Not a number manually nudged up or down (Counter) or an amount completed toward a goal (Ring).
- Cart: Review and edit what you are about to buy. Pick: A shopping basket before ordering, with editable quantities, removal, a promo code and computed totals. Not simple rows (List), an already placed order (OrderSummary), or a grocery checklist (GroceryList).
- CartBar: Return to a nonempty basket from a shopping screen. Pick: A persistent bottom shortcut to the basket with its live count and total, hidden when empty. Not a lone action without live basket data (Button) or the editable basket itself (Cart).
- Checkout: Choose fulfillment and payment, then place an order. Pick: Finish a goods order by choosing pickup or delivery and a payment method, then place it. Not editing one field (Field), reviewing an appointment (Appointment), or editing basket items (Cart).
- OrderStatus: Follow an order through fulfillment or move it along as the seller. Pick: Track fulfillment milestones on one goods order, with timestamps and a seller's next-stage action. Not a multi-step form (Steps), a map (DeliveryTracker), or an order receipt (OrderSummary).
- OrderSummary: See what was ordered, what it cost and how it will arrive. Pick: A receipt for one placed goods order with quantities and fulfillment details. Not simple facts (KeyValue), the editable basket (Cart), fulfillment progress (OrderStatus), or a client bill (Invoice).
- Product: Decide whether to buy one product and add the desired quantity. Pick: One product for sale with a description, stock, saving or quantity and add controls. Not a price alone (Amount), several products (ProductGrid), or a timed service (ServiceMenu).
- ProductGrid: Browse products with prices and quickly add the ones you want. Pick: Browse several priced goods with a quick add per product, as photo cards or food menu rows. Not photos without prices (Gallery), timed services (ServiceMenu), or owned things (Things).
- Promo: Notice an offer, copy its discount code or open the offer. Pick: A shop discount or offer with optional copyable code, expiry and product photo. Not an urgent warning or service notice (Banner) or a headline fact (Hero).
- VariantPicker: Choose an available size, colour or other option for one product. Pick: Select the variant of one product, with optional price differences and disabled unavailable options. Not choosing a plan (Choice) or filtering a product list (Chips).

Need, in the person's words: "Choose between monthly and annual membership plans with prices and a description of each plan"
Reply with only the component id, nothing else.

5d1ffa75b20dfc95.prompt:
You choose the one UI component that best fits a need on a phone app screen.
Components:
- Actions: Two to four shortcuts to different things the person can do next. Pick: Two to four separate navigation shortcuts together, such as logging, adding and viewing a schedule. Not independent jobs to tick off (Checklist), one main action (Button), or records to browse (List).
- Amount: One sum of money written properly, with its period, old price or change. Pick: One sum of money is the point: a balance, a price, a total or what is owed. Not several figures side by side (Stats), the screen's headline in words (Hero), or the price on each row of a list (List).
- Banner: Something important to notice now, with an optional link to act. Pick: An immediate warning or status update that stands out at the top. Not a supporting sentence (Note), the screen's main statement (Hero) or a panel with more detail (Sheet).
- Bars: Compare counts or amounts across days or categories, using the actual counted or measured unit. Pick: Compare one amount across days or categories. Not a few separate summary numbers (Stats), a trend with its latest value (Sparkline) or progress toward targets (Progress).
- Bubbles: A conversation between you and someone else, with each person's messages kept distinct. Pick: Show an exchange between you and another person, keeping who said each message clear. Not things to browse and tap (List) or one supporting sentence without a reply (Note).
- Button: One main thing the person does next. Pick: One labelled action to press. Not two to four shortcuts (Actions) or a tappable summary of one thing (Card).
- Calendar: See which dates have something planned and open a day. Pick: Days of a week or month, with dates marked for planned activity. Not events with times in order (Timeline) or separate things to browse (List).
- Camera: Aim at something and take a new picture or scan its code. Pick: Take a new picture or scan a code while aiming at the subject. Not showing an existing picture (Photo), or adding a picture to a labelled form value (Field).
- Canvas: An idea no existing component can express, such as a game or a drawing tool. Pick: Only choose Canvas for an idea no other component can express, such as an interactive game or a drawing tool. Not a message about missing content (Empty), or an existing image to display (Photo).
- Card: One thing with a little detail, optionally tappable to open it. Pick: A compact preview of one thing, with a title and short detail, optionally opening it. Not several separate things to scan (List) or the screen's main headline (Hero).
- Checklist: Things to do, with each job ticked off when done. Pick: Tick off independent jobs. Not browsing and opening things (List) or following an ordered sequence (Steps).
- Chips: Filter things or pick one value from a few short options. Pick: Filter a collection or choose a value. Not switching between views (Segmented), ticking off jobs (Checklist) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- Choice: Choose among two to five options that each need a sentence to explain. Pick: Choosing among a few options that each carry a short explanation, such as a plan, an answer to a question or a way of doing something. Not one-word filters (Chips), a short value inside a form (Field), switching views of one screen (Segmented), or keep-or-skip one at a time (SwipeStack).
- Composer: Write several lines of text: an entry, a note, a review or a reply. Pick: Writing more than one line, such as a journal entry, a note, a review or a reply under a conversation. Not one short value on a form (Field), or finding something by name (Search).
- Counter: Increase or decrease one running count by a fixed step with each tap. Pick: One count whose plus button increments and minus button decrements the number by a fixed step. Not several read-only summary numbers (Stats) or a number entered in a form (Field).
- Empty: A calm message on a screen that has no content yet. Pick: Only when there is no content or no results yet, explaining their absence. Not the screen's main statement about what exists or needs attention (Hero), a separate warning or status notice (Banner), or a supporting sentence (Note).
- Field: Enter or change one labelled piece of information on a form. Pick: Enter one named value, such as a name, date, amount or form choice. Not finding things by typing a query (Search), standalone collection filters and quick choices (Chips), several lines of writing (Composer) or options that each need a sentence (Choice).
- Gallery: Browse several pictures together, optionally opening one. Pick: Several pictures to browse together, in a grid or sideways strip. Not one picture on its own (Photo) or text-led rows of separate things (List).
- Header: Name the screen and offer one optional shortcut. Pick: The title at the top of a screen. Not a label above a group (SectionTitle) or the screen's main message (Hero).
- Hero: The screen's main statement or headline number, including what needs attention today. Pick: The screen's main message, photo-led introduction or headline number, even when it says something needs attention. Not a separate urgent alert or status update (Banner), a supporting sentence (Note), several numbers (Stats) or one sum of money as the point (Amount).
- KeyValue: Label and value details of one single thing, like its room or schedule. Pick: Any need about one thing's details or settings. Not several separate things (List) or summary numbers (Stats).
- List: Several things of the same kind, each one tappable. Pick: Several things of one kind to scan and tap individually, even when asked to tap just one of them. Not one featured thing (Card), details of one thing (KeyValue), or jobs to tick off (Checklist).
- MapPins: See where nearby places are and open a place. Pick: Places positioned on a map, with matching numbered labels and optional links. Not places visited in travel order (Route) or things to browse without their locations on a map (List).
- Note: One short sentence of supporting information. Pick: Add a short supporting sentence. Not something to notice now (Banner), the screen's main statement (Hero) or text the person writes (Composer).
- People: Who else is involved, with their names and roles. Pick: The clients, family or team involved, with a name and optional role for each person. Not general things to scan and tap (List), or the identity of one screen's subject (Profile).
